title: The private operator console
implementation_status: PARTIAL PREPARATION — interface prototype; not connected to real service state
accepted_note: Claude authored, ran and looked at this. Self-testing is not independent acceptance, and 'independently tested usability' in particular is NOT satisfied: no person other than the author has used it.

gate.also_exercised: Run for real (console/run.py) and driven in a browser: sign-in, dashboard, limit-change preparation and the prepared-change page were rendered and read, not just asserted.

what_the_console_cannot_do.statement: It holds no keys and broadcasts nothing. It cannot fence, activate, sign or send.
what_the_console_cannot_do.why: Those are owner and runner authorities. A console that held them would be a fourth authority over customer funds that the P04 authority inventory does not contain.
what_the_console_cannot_do.instead: It READS state and PREPARES a described owner action, which the owner executes in their own Safe. Every prepared change records executed_by_console=false.
what_the_console_cannot_do.this_is_also_the_approval_design: The owner approves a described change -- 'the supply ceiling drops from 50,000 to 8,000 USDC, 17,500 is already spent, so 0 remains, and nothing else changes' -- rather than a calldata blob. 'What does NOT change' is stated as prominently as what does, because that is the real question when approving.

authentication_and_privacy.binding: 127.0.0.1 only. Binding elsewhere raises ConsoleNotPrivate unless explicitly overridden, because a network-reachable console is a different product with a different threat model.
authentication_and_privacy.secret: An env:NAME REFERENCE, never a literal. An absent secret is refused; one shorter than 16 characters is refused.
authentication_and_privacy.comparison: hmac.compare_digest, so a wrong secret cannot be recovered by timing. Asserted by a test that reads the source.
authentication_and_privacy.sessions: In-memory, one-hour TTL, not persisted -- a restart logs everyone out. Expired cookies do not authenticate.
authentication_and_privacy.csrf: State-changing forms carry a token bound to the session; a missing or wrong token is refused with 403.
authentication_and_privacy.escaping: Every interpolated value is escaped; a hostile controller address renders as text, verified by test.
authentication_and_privacy.headers: Verified over real HTTP: X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Referrer-Policy no-referrer, Content-Security-Policy default-src 'none'. The session cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict.
authentication_and_privacy.no_partial_reads: An unauthenticated request to any route returns a 302 with an EMPTY body. There is no read-only peek.
authentication_and_privacy.logging: Request logging strips query strings, which can carry a CSRF token.

recovery_export.contents: Every unresolved operation with its payload hash, state, epoch and attempts.
recovery_export.no_secrets: Signer fields are REFERENCES (env:NAME, keystore:path). Verified by a test that writes a real journal row and asserts no key material and no console secret appears in the export.
recovery_export.instructions_included: How to resolve each case, including the ambiguous one: read consumed[operationId]; equal to payload_hash means it executed and must never be re-executed; zero after a definitive refusal means it may be reauthorized under a new epoch; zero after an ambiguous send means it may still be in flight -- re-read, do not resend.

defects_found_by_looking_at_it.what: The operator-action links rendered near-black on the dark background and were close to invisible.
defects_found_by_looking_at_it.found_by: Rendering the page in a browser. No test would have caught it; every assertion about those links passed.
defects_found_by_looking_at_it.fix: Explicit link, visited, hover and focus colours.

known_gaps: Independently tested usability is NOT satisfied: only the author has used it. This is one of several gaps, and not the largest — the connection to real service state matters more.
console/run.py renders a DEMONSTRATION state when no state source is given, labelled as such in the module docstring. It is not a reading of any deployed controller and is not evidence about one.
The live state provider is an injected callable. Wiring it to a real chain reader is straightforward but is not done here, so the dashboard has not yet displayed a reading of the fork.

Implicit form submission (pressing Return) could not be exercised through the browser automation. The form is standard HTML with a submit button and the button works; this is most likely an automation artifact rather than a page defect, and it is recorded as unverified rather than claimed either way.
Nothing is deployed and the console is not served anywhere. It binds to localhost on demand.
completeness: PARTIAL PREPARATION. A working private console prototype with real authentication, privacy and escaping, not yet the connected operator product V4 §8 specifies.
next: P06 composed adversarial faults and the Held half of the frozen comparison.

reclassified_by_review.authoritative_views_exist: V4 §8 specifies Terms / Activity / Change & handover / Authority & export. The console instead implemented four views DERIVED from the product sentence, because the locked plan was not in the repository. The plan is now restored under docs/plan/ and the derived J1-J4 labels are demoted to explanatory shorthand.
still_missing: The four §8 views as specified, with their required data and actions.

Real service state. console/run.py always constructs Console(demonstration_state, journal): its docstring advertises a --state-source argument the parser does not define, so the delivered entry point can pair a REAL journal with hardcoded balances, runner and Active/epoch.
An operator-visible demonstration banner. A disclaimer in a module docstring is not a label the operator sees.

An actual unsigned, state-bound Safe owner transaction. Keeping owner keys out of the console is correct, but generating a state-bound candidate transaction does NOT give the console owner authority, and PreparedChange currently carries prose only.
Organization / Safe / lineage binding and finalized-block binding in the state model.
A complete replacement/recovery export: the current export carries unresolved operations but not the full replacement context, and its docstring promises tombstones it does not include.
reclassified_by_review.prerequisite_not_met: P05 depends on P04 services, which depend on the P03 route. Neither is established.

defect_found_by_review.what: The interrupted-operations reading described AUTHORIZED as 'Signed, but nothing was sent' and 'Safe to send or to abandon', without consulting pending attempts.
defect_found_by_review.why_it_matters: After a crash mid-send the operation can read AUTHORIZED while a claimed attempt is outstanding. Telling an operator 'nothing was sent' there invites a hand-authorised duplicate submission.
defect_found_by_review.status: FIXED — an unresolved attempt now overrides the state wording with 'A submission was claimed and may have reached the executor. This is NOT nothing was sent', and directs the operator to read consumed[operationId] and RESUME the original attempt rather than start a new one.

the_four_views.authoritative_source: V4 §8, restored at docs/plan/14_Held_Locked_V4.md: Terms / Activity / Change & handover / Authority & export.
the_four_views.what_was_built_instead: Four views derived from the product sentence (J1-J4). The derivation was reasonable and is not useless -- it maps onto the same operator tasks -- but it was the wrong move: the authoritative list existed and should have been requested rather than reconstructed.
the_four_views.current_state: The J-labels survive as explanatory shorthand for the operator task each surface serves, and are useful for naming tests. They do NOT stand in for the §8 views, whose required data and actions are not yet implemented.

mapping.Terms: partially covered by the dashboard's limits table (ceilings, Used, Remaining, cooldowns). Missing: market and supported actions, floor, and precise pending changes.
mapping.Activity: partially covered by the interrupted-operations view. Missing: HOLD/refusal/submitted/executed rows, KeeperHub attempt and transaction/effect evidence.
mapping.Change & handover: partially covered by the limit-change and runner-replacement preparation. Missing: fence status, owner cleanup, candidate terms and missing-input reporting.
mapping.Authority & export: partially covered by the recovery export. Missing: scope/block/finality, complete/incomplete sections, and the full offline recovery package.
